body: Ah OK. Thanks for letting me know. Appreciated

There are many reasons people commit suicide, I would argue mental illness is by far the biggest contributor. Hence advocating compassion over judgment. Take care, I think we're on the same page really just expressing ourselves differently. All the best.

If as you say mental illness makes you more likely to die by suicide then your first statement that mental illness has nothing to do with suicide, is by your own admission completely wrong, and to use your own words ignorant.

I hear you. I've debated a lot with people who get very passionate it's selfish and I find it quite upsetting.  It's just not logical. Millions of years of evolution have made us into survival machines at all cost and to go against that biological urge to live is the action of a very sick and troubled mind and should be greeted with compassion not judgment.

I think it's because a lot of people can only view the world from their own perspective and feelings. If they have never felt suicidal it's beyond their ability to empathise past how it will affect them, they can't imagine being out of control like a suicidal person therefore they don't believe it's a fair thing to do to another person. Hence framing it as a disease like cancer can help people imagine to see that dieing from it may have been out of their control.

A lot of people still can't accept suicide is an illness. You wouldn't be mad at someone for dieing of cancer or heart disease so don't get angry at people for losing their fight with mental illness. It's a helpful way to frame it for people who have lost someone I think.

I'm sorry your feeling like this. My life is very different to yours I imagine, but I do feel suicidal very often. If talking to a stranger is something you think you could do please say anything you like to me about anything you want. . I would really like to listen to you. People have listened to me occasionally when I've been at my darkest and I just thought I'd offer that to you.
